intro.title: Anxiety Type Test
intro.subtitle: What Kind of Worrier Are You?
intro.boundary: This author-created activity is for private reflection. It does not diagnose anxiety or any health condition.

question.0: When you have an important event tomorrow, you...
question.1: You sent a message but they haven't replied in hours, you...
question.2: Your boss says 'Can we talk?' with no context, you...
question.3: You're about to give a presentation, you...
question.4: You notice an unexplained pain in your body, you...
question.5: Plans suddenly change at the last minute, you...
question.6: You made a small mistake at work, you...
question.7: You're lying in bed at night trying to sleep, you...
question.0a: Lie awake replaying every possible scenario in your head over and over
question.0b: Obsessively prepare and double-check everything until it's perfect
question.0c: Worry about what people will think of you and how you'll come across
question.0d: Feel your heart racing, stomach churning, and can't physically relax
question.0e: Imagine all the things that could go wrong and spiral into dread
question.0f: Make detailed checklists and backup plans for every contingency
question.1a: Reread your message 50 times analyzing what you said wrong
question.1b: Regret not wording it more perfectly and draft better versions
question.1c: Convince yourself they're upset with you or talking about you
question.1d: Feel a knot in your stomach and check your phone obsessively
question.1e: Assume the worst — they hate you, the friendship is over
question.1f: Feel uneasy because the situation is out of your control
question.2a: Mentally review every task you've done, searching for mistakes
question.2b: Immediately worry you haven't been performing well enough
question.2c: Panic about being singled out and what colleagues will think
question.2d: Feel instant chest tightness and your palms get sweaty
question.2e: Jump to 'I'm getting fired' and start catastrophizing your future
question.2f: Feel frustrated that they didn't give you context to prepare
question.3a: Can't stop thinking about every possible question they might ask
question.3b: Revise your slides for the 20th time because nothing feels good enough
question.3c: Feel terrified of being judged and want to disappear
question.3d: Feel dizzy, nauseous, and your hands are trembling
question.3e: Dread everything that could go wrong during the presentation
question.3f: Need to control every technical detail and seating arrangement
question.4a: Spend hours researching symptoms and reading medical articles
question.4b: Worry that you haven't been taking care of yourself properly
question.4c: Avoid telling anyone because you don't want to seem dramatic
question.4d: Immediately feel panicked — your heart races and breathing quickens
question.4e: Imagine the worst diagnosis and plan for terrible outcomes
question.4f: Schedule a doctor's appointment immediately so you can have answers
question.5a: Get stuck in your head trying to process and adapt to the new plan
question.5b: Feel frustrated because the original plan was better organized
question.5c: Worry about how you'll fit in or perform in the new situation
question.5d: Feel physically uncomfortable — tense muscles, uneasy stomach
question.5e: Immediately worry about what else might go wrong today
question.5f: Feel deeply unsettled and anxious without a clear plan
question.6a: Replay it in your mind for days, analyzing what you should have done
question.6b: Beat yourself up because you should have caught it before it happened
question.6c: Worry that everyone noticed and thinks less of you now
question.6d: Feel a wave of heat, stomach drop, and physical shame response
question.6e: Catastrophize that this mistake will snowball into bigger problems
question.6f: Immediately create a system to make sure it never happens again
question.7a: Your mind races through everything that happened today and tomorrow's tasks
question.7b: Review whether you did everything well enough and what you could improve
question.7c: Replay social interactions and worry about how others perceived you
question.7d: Feel restless — your body is tense and you can't find a comfortable position
question.7e: Worry about the future and feel a vague sense of dread about what's coming
question.7f: Plan tomorrow down to the minute because uncertainty keeps you awake

result.boundary: This summary only counts the choices you made here. It is not a diagnosis, a validated assessment, or proof of how you respond in every situation.
result.calculation: How it works: each answer adds one point to a worry-response label. The label selected most often is shown above; ties use the earliest matching label.
